acceptable_paraphrases: Shapes can have more than one line of symmetry.
critical_errors: Incorrectly stating that only squares have equal opposite sides.
Claiming that a test with fewer than four right angles and no lines of symmetry is valid for identifying squares.
Forgetting to mention that non-square rhombuses also have exactly two lines of symmetry.
misconceptions: Thinking that only squares have equal opposite sides.
Believing that a test with fewer than four right angles and no lines of symmetry can definitively identify a square.
grading_notes: Focus on the core concepts related to shape properties. Credit for identifying common misconceptions in Viktor's comments, such as the equal sides property of parallelograms and non-square rhombuses having two lines of symmetry.
